paths.description: Workspace-relative paths to include in the archive.

ConfigResponse.description: `GET /api/config` body: feature flags the OWUI terminal UI connection-gates on.

ContentMatch.description: One content match inside a file: line, UTF-16 code-unit column, line text.

column.description: 1-indexed column in UTF-16 code units (upstream mirror).

text.description: The matched line, trimmed of its line terminator.

CreateSandboxRequest.description: `POST /api/sandboxes` body: instantiate a Sandbox from a template.

oneOf.description: Persistence profile; defaults to `BROKER_DEFAULT_PROFILE` when omitted.

sessionId.description: Owning session/chat id (recorded as the `broker-session` annotation).

templateName.description: Name of the backing `SandboxTemplate` to clone the pod blueprint from.

userId.description: Owning user id (recorded as the `broker-user` annotation).

CwdRequest.description: Request body for `POST /files/cwd`: the workspace-relative directory to switch to.

path.description: Workspace-relative directory to make the effective cwd.

Entry.description: One entry in a directory listing (name, type, size, modified time, writability).

writable.description: Whether the entry is writable (0.11.35 open-terminal contract: `access(W_OK)`).

ErrorResponse.description:
Error body both control planes return: `{"detail": "..."}` (the
`{ "detail": <string> }` shape — byte-for-byte parity, D11). Used as the
error response `body` across the broker and runtime `OpenAPI` surfaces.

ExecuteRequest.description:
`POST /execute` request body. `timeout` is clamped into `[1, MAX_TIMEOUT]`,
defaulting to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (seconds).

timeout.description: Optional wall-clock timeout in seconds (clamped into `[1, MAX_TIMEOUT]`).

ExecuteResponse.description: `POST /execute` response body (HTTP 200 even on non-zero exit).

exit_code.description: Process exit code (HTTP 200 even when non-zero; `124` on timeout).

timed_out.description: Whether the command was killed for exceeding `timeout`.

FileUpload.description:
Typed `multipart/form-data` body for the upload endpoints: a single binary
`file` part. The runtime consumes the stream directly via
`axum::extract::Multipart` (this struct exists only to describe the wire
contract for OpenAPI/Scalar — it is never deserialized). The on-disk name
is the basename of the part's `Content-Disposition` `filename`; path
components are stripped as defense-in-depth (see `upload_basename`).

ListResponse.description: A directory listing: the resolved directory, its writability, and sorted entries.

writable.description: Whether the listed directory itself is writable (0.11.35).

MatchResult.description: One unified-search row (name match, content matches, or both).

content_matches.description: Literal content matches inside the file (<= 3).

relative_path.description: Path relative to the search directory (`/`-separated).

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page, or `None` when exhausted.

destination.description: Workspace-relative destination path (must not already exist).

source.description: Workspace-relative path of the entry to move.

OperatingMode.description:
`spec.operatingMode` — the upstream controller's lifecycle mode.

Serializes as the upstream string literals `Running` / `Suspended` (serde's
default unit-variant representation), matching the values patched in
`_set_sandbox_operating_mode`.

PathBody.description: Request body carrying a single workspace-relative path (`mkdir`, etc.).

Profile.description:
Persistence profile — what backing volume a sandbox gets.

Serializes as the lowercase literals `persistent` / `ephemeral` (D12 — the
values honoured by `BROKER_DEFAULT_PROFILE` and the `X-Persistence`
header). Defaults to [`Profile::Persistent`], the broker deploy default.

ReplaceRequest.description: Request body for `POST /files/replace`: apply find/replace chunks to one file.

replacements.description: Ordered find/replace chunks applied to the file.

ReplacementChunk.description: One find/replace chunk applied to a workspace file.

allow_multiple.description: When `true`, replace every occurrence; otherwise require exactly one match.

end_line.description: Optional inclusive 1-based end line for a line-scoped replacement.

start_line.description: Optional 1-based start line for a line-scoped replacement.

RestoreResponse.description:
Response body for `PUT /restore`: whether the workspace was restored and the
compressed bytes ingested. `restored: false` with `skipped:
Some("workspace-non-empty")` is the #142 hot-tier hit: the caller (broker)
asked for a cold restore, but the mounted workspace already has data (PVC
park-resume), and unpacking the cold object over it could regress newer
state — so the runtime declines and keeps serving the hot tier.

SandboxCondition.description:
A status condition as surfaced in [`SandboxStatus::conditions`] (mirrors the
upstream `meta.v1.Condition` subset read for readiness).

SandboxObject.description:
`OpenAPI` schema for a `Sandbox` object on the wire (`apiVersion`/`kind`/`metadata`/
`spec`/`status`). The CRUD handlers return the kube-generated [`shared::Sandbox`] (an
identical shape); this broker-local schema surfaces the typed spec/status in the
generated document (issue #75).

oneOf.description: Last-observed status (conditions, pod IPs, …); absent until reconciled.

SandboxSpec.description:
Spec of a [`Sandbox`] — a running tenant sandbox managed by the broker.

`operatingMode` / `shutdownPolicy` are typed because the broker parks a
sandbox (`Suspended`) and resumes it (`Running`) and relies on
`shutdownPolicy: Retain` to keep the object across a park. `podTemplate` is
the opaque per-instance pod blueprint cloned from the backing
[`SandboxTemplate`] (see the module docs for why it is untyped).

oneOf.description:
Lifecycle mode the upstream controller honours. `Running` (default) keeps
the pod scheduled; `Suspended` parks it (pod deleted, object retained) so
a later resume reuses the same identity + per-session Secret.

podTemplate.description:
Opaque per-instance pod blueprint, cloned from the backing
[`SandboxTemplate`] and shuffled by the broker (volumes, labels).

oneOf.description:
Whether the `Sandbox` object is retained after its pod exits. The broker
sets `Retain` so a parked sandbox survives to be resumed rather than
recreated.

templateName.description: Name of the [`SandboxTemplate`] backing this sandbox.

SandboxStatus.description:
Status of a [`Sandbox`] — the subset of fields the broker reads (readiness +
pod IP) plus the common scalars it forwards. Authored here so readiness can
be computed in typed Rust rather than by poking raw JSON.

conditions.description: Status conditions; a `Ready`/`True` entry means the sandbox is serving.

podIPs.description: Pod IPs assigned to the sandbox; `[0]` is the address the broker proxies to.

ready.description: Convenience readiness flag, when the controller surfaces it.

SearchResult.description: One ranked result row (`path` is absolute, matching upstream).

path.description: Absolute path of the match (upstream returns absolute paths).

ShutdownPolicy.description: `spec.shutdownPolicy` — whether the `Sandbox` object survives its pod exiting.

TermInfo.description: Public info for a terminal session — the `GET /api/terminals` JSON body.

WriteRequest.description: Request body for `POST /files/write`: overwrite a file with the given content.

content.description: Full text content to write to the file.

path.description: Workspace-relative file to overwrite (parents created as needed).

info.description: Open WebUI front door + Kubernetes Sandbox lifecycle. The runtime tool surface (/execute, /files/*, /snapshot, /restore, /api/terminals*) is proxied to the resolved sandbox pod and documented here as part of the OWUI-facing contract. The catch-all reverse proxy (/{*path}) and the /api/terminals/{id} WebSocket upgrade are opaque passthroughs omitted from this document (issue #75 Q5).
info.title: open-websandbox broker

post.summary:
`POST /api/sandboxes` — create a `Sandbox` from a `SandboxTemplate` (C-1
foundation; C-2's resolve-on-request reuses this path). 201 on create, 200
with the existing object on a 409 — idempotent (409 → update existing).

`GET /api/status` — operator telemetry (static until C-2/C-4 make it real).

get.description:
# Errors

Currently always returns `Ok`; the `Result` keeps the handler signature
uniform with the other `/api/terminals` endpoints.
get.summary: `GET /api/terminals` — list live sessions, reaping any dead ones observed.

post.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError`] (via [`request_base`]) for an invalid workspace
subdir, [`ApiError::TooManyRequests`] when the session cap is reached, and
[`ApiError::ServiceUnavailable`] if the PTY shell fails to spawn.

200.description: PTY session spawned (or recreated) — idempotent, returns 200 on create-or-recreate

post.summary: `POST /api/terminals` — spawn a new PTY shell session.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /api/terminals/{id}` — kill + reap the session. Idempotent: an unknown id
still answers `200 {"status":"deleted"}`.

200.description: Session info for non-upgrade requests (the WebSocket upgrade relay is omitted from this document)

get.summary:
`GET /api/terminals/{id}` — either the JSON info endpoint, or (when the request
carries the WebSocket upgrade headers) the PTY relay. `Authed` runs first, so a
missing/invalid Bearer is rejected with 401 BEFORE the socket is accepted.

`GET /docs` — the Scalar API reference UI, served by `utoipa-scalar` and inlining
`/openapi.json` (issue #75 Q3).

[`ApiError::Internal`] on a read failure.

post.description:
`Authed` authenticates the per-session key; `HeaderMap` carries the optional
`X-Workspace-Subdir`; `Json` parses the body (body-consuming extractor last).

get.description:
# Errors

post.description:
# Panics

Panics only if the static `application/zip` / `Content-Disposition` header
values fail to parse, which cannot happen for these constants.
post.summary:
`POST /files/archive` — zip the listed paths and stream the archive back.
Dirs recurse (files archived as `<basename>/<rel>`); a single file archives
as its basename. `application/zip` + `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

get.summary: Return the effective workspace cwd (== home) for the session.

post.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace and
[`ApiError::NotFound`] if it is missing or not a directory.
post.summary: Set the session cwd to a workspace-relative directory.

delete.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace or the
removal fails, and [`ApiError::NotFound`] if the path is missing.
delete.summary: Delete a workspace file or directory (recursively).

get.description:
This is a **signaling** endpoint, not a byte-serving one: upstream
`display_file` (open_terminal/main.py @ v0.12.3) resolves the path and
reports `exists`; the consuming client opens its own viewer. A missing
file is a successful `exists: false` response — only an invalid path
errors. Divergence: ours confines the resolved path to the workspace
(400 on escape) like every other file endpoint; upstream single-user
mode resolves arbitrary host paths.

# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace.
get.summary: Signal that a file should be shown to the user (upstream 0.2.9 contract).

get.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace and
[`ApiError::NotFound`] if the search directory is missing.
get.summary: Glob-match workspace entries by pattern and optional type.

get.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace or the
regex is invalid, and [`ApiError::NotFound`] if the search path is missing.
get.summary: Grep the workspace for a literal or regex query.

get.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace,
[`ApiError::NotFound`] if it is missing or not a directory, and
[`ApiError::Internal`] if the directory cannot be read.

parameters.description: Optional workspace-relative directory to list (defaults to `.`).
parameters.name: directory

get.summary: List the entries of a workspace-relative directory.

get.description:
Score 0 = exact name, 1 = name prefix, 2 = name contains,
3 = relative path contains, 4 = content-only. Sorted by
`(score, relative_path.len(), relative path lowercase)` and paginated
with `next_offset`.

# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] for a blank query or out-of-range
`offset`/`limit`, and [`ApiError::NotFound`] when `path` is missing or
not a directory.
get.summary: Unified search by ranked name, path, and content (0.12.0).

post.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace or the
directory cannot be created.
post.summary: Create a workspace directory (and missing parents).

post.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if either path escapes the workspace or
the rename fails, [`ApiError::NotFound`] if the source is missing, and
[`ApiError::Conflict`] if the destination already exists.

get.description:
Mirrors the open-terminal 0.2.7 contract: optional 1-indexed inclusive
`start_line`/`end_line` slicing for text; images return raw bytes; any
other non-UTF-8 binary returns 415 (Office/text extraction deferred —
see docs/compatibility.md).

# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace or a
line range is zero, [`ApiError::NotFound`] if it is missing or not a regular
file, [`ApiError::UnsupportedMediaType`] for non-image binaries, and
[`ApiError::Internal`] on a read failure.

200.description: File content (JSON) or raw image bytes

get.summary: Read a workspace file as JSON text, or raw bytes for an image.

post.description:
# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace, the
read/write fails, or a replacement target is missing/ambiguous, and
[`ApiError::NotFound`] if the file is missing.
post.summary: Apply one or more find/replace chunks to a workspace file.

get.description:
Rank 0 = exact name (case-insensitive), 1 = name prefix, 2 = substring;
an empty `query` matches everything at rank 2. Sort key
`(rank, name.len(), relative path lowercase)` — the upstream order.

# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] for an out-of-range `limit` or bad
`type`, and [`ApiError::NotFound`] when `path` is missing or not a directory.
get.summary: Search files and subdirectories by ranked filename match (0.11.36).

get.description:
Path-parameter alias of the view semantics introduced by open-terminal
0.11.34 so OWUI FileNav iframes resolve relative assets. Unlike
[`view_file`] there is **no** `Content-Disposition: attachment` header —
browsers must render the bytes inline.

# Errors

Returns [`ApiError::BadRequest`] if the path escapes the workspace and
[`ApiError::NotFound`] if it is missing or not a regular file.

200.description: Raw file bytes with guessed content type

get.summary: Serve a workspace file inline with its guessed content type.

get.summary:
`GET /list` + `GET /list/` — list the workspace root. The route
`/list/{file_path:path}` matches the empty path (lists root); axum's
`/list/{*file_path}` catch-all requires ≥1 segment, so these explicit routes
cover the empty-path case (parity, D11).

metric catalogue (`open_websandbox_broker_*`: HTTP rate/latency, active
sandboxes, sandbox create/delete counts, runtime-hop errors) in
`text/plain; version=0.0.4`.

get.description:

one document. `info.version` is pinned to the crate version (issue #75 Q4) and the
structural shape is guarded by a frozen-snapshot test (issue #75 Q2).
get.summary: `GET /openapi.json` — the curated method surface OWUI discovers tools from.

feeds both endpoints; ours does too).

`GET /readyz` — the apiserver (hard dependency for sandbox resolution) is
reachable. 503 when not, so the Service stops routing to a broker that would
only 500.
